defense_in_depth_findings.title: GO-token census enforced by parsed-object equality rather than canonical token bytes
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: scripts/research/f017_representative_ffn_composition_release_wrapper_v2.py authorize() enforces the eight-field token census via dict equality against the expected object (duplicate keys rejected by the unique object_pairs_hook), so token byte-level canonicalization and key order are not constrained. Independently exercised the committed authorize() at head 232d19d7573701805c683d7d02278ea21b956ebd: missing-field, extra-field (including a direct release_review_sha256 field), wrong-disposition, forged-approval-sha, v1-release-sha, real_event_authorized=false, and wrong-attempt-id tokens all reject with GO_TOKEN; no authority is lost because approval_sha256 binds the exact approval bytes and the census is exact.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_action: None for v2. If a future revision records the token hash into durable state semantics beyond attempt-start, consider requiring canonical_json token bytes for uniform hashing.

statement: REPRESENTATIVE FFN COMPOSITION SINGLE-USE RELEASE V2 APPROVAL ACCEPTED
